newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UN agency says Angola denies it access to refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN agency says Angola denies it access to refugees.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) in Angola said on Wednesday the Angolan government had denied its officials access to thousands of Rwandan refugees camped along the northern border with Zaire.
"We need to get basic information on the situation," UNHCR representative in Luanda, Marjon Kamara, told reporters.
"We need to know how many people are there, what they need, what their condition is. Unfortunately, we have not been allowed to enter the area to find these things," she added.

Angola's Minister of Assistance and Social Reintegration Albino Malungo, who is overseeing the refugee problem, said at the weekend he believed up to 17,000 Rwandan refugees were just north of the border with Zaire and many were armed.
The U.N.'s peacekeeping mission in Angola, UNAVEM, has also been denied access to the area where the refugees are camped, near the city of Dundo in the diamond-rich Lunda Norte province.
The UNHCR said it had reports that the Angolan government was forcibly removing refugees who have managed to cross the border into Lunda Norte.
It said there was evidence that many of the refugees at the border, fleeing fighting in their homeland, are in poor condition and some are dying.

Last month the UNHCR said in Geneva it believed about 30,000 Rwandan refugees, many thought to be members of the former Hutu-led army and Interhamwe militia, largely held responsible for the 1994 Rwandan genocide, were seen moving towards the Angolan border.
